The image of the nebula was assembled from exposures taken in five filters spanning the near-infrared, each chosen to isolate a different emission line or continuum band. Individual exposures of 800 seconds were dithered by sub-pixel offsets to recover resolution lost to undersampling, then combined using a drizzle algorithm that weights each input pixel by its noise properties. Cosmic-ray hits were identified by comparing the stack of frames and rejected before combination. Color was applied by assigning the shortest wavelength filter to blue and the longest to red; because the data lie outside the visible range, the resulting palette is a mapping, not a literal view. The brightest filaments correspond to ionized hydrogen, while the darker lanes trace dust grains absorbing background light. Photometric calibration was performed against standard stars observed in the same program, yielding flux uncertainties of about three percent across the field.
